_README: THE KANJO LOADER — two cars trading position on a night highway.
THE VEHICLE ART SHIPPING HERE IS TEMPORARY AND NEUTRAL. car-a.svg and
car-b.svg are unbranded silhouettes: no badge, no grille, no real car. They
exist so the choreography has something to move. Replacing them is a change
to this file and nothing else — drop the final art in public/media/loader/
and point carA/carB at it. Width and height are the art's INTRINSIC pixel
size and are what stop the loader from reflowing as the images decode.
TIMING. minimumDisplayMs is a floor so a warm cache does not turn the
entrance into a flicker; one full overtake takes about 3s, so ~2200 shows a
complete trade of position. maximumDisplayMs is the ESCAPE PATH: past it
the site opens whatever is still loading. The maximum always wins if the two
are ever set to disagree.
WHAT 'READY' MEANS: hydration plus the display font. NOT every asset on the
page — a loader that waits for the hero video is a loader a slow connection
can hold open for a minute.
intensity: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'. A phone automatically runs one step
below whatever is set here, and prefers-reduced-motion replaces the whole
sequence with a still frame and a short fade.
road: optional. A painted plate behind the generated surface. Omitted, the
highway is drawn from CSS alone and costs no request at all.

_comment: V1 LANDING PAGE — deliberately short.
The order is the experience: THE KANJO, what it is, watch it, read the
development log. Four blocks and a footer, over a loader. A visitor should
be able to take the whole site in without deciding to.
EVERY BLOCK THE LONGER PAGE CARRIED STILL EXISTS. Features, development
status, the screenshot gallery, the local-video block and the links panel
are all still in the registry and still configurable — they are switched
off below. Turning one back on is `published: true` and an `order`; it is
not a code change. Nothing was deleted, and nothing extra is on the page.
COPY STATUS: anything containing the word PLACEHOLDER is NOT RENDERED — see
lib/content/placeholder.ts. A section with unwritten copy shows less rather
than showing an instruction to the site's owner. The inventory of what is
still needed is docs/CONTENT_REQUIRED.md.

_README: HERO MEDIA. The canon's own composition is media + dim + UI
(UI_Canon/Screens/MainMenu/layout.json defaultTreatment.mode = 'dim').
kind is 'none' only because no footage exists yet. The hero already
reserves the full media footprint and applies the dim, so switching is a
CONTENT change with no layout change and no component edit.
A STILL — copy the export to public/media/hero/, then:
"kind": "image",
"image": { "src": "/media/hero/hero.jpg", "alt": "",
"treatment": "dim"
A LOOP — MP4 always, WebM as well if you can. A poster is MANDATORY:
it is the first paint, the fallback if the loop cannot play, and what
shows under prefers-reduced-motion, where the video is not rendered.
"kind": "video",
"videoSources": ["/media/hero/loop.webm", "/media/hero/loop.mp4"],
"poster": { "src": "/media/hero/loop-poster.jpg", "alt": "",
"treatment": "dim"
FRAMING. objectPosition is a plain CSS object-position: 'center 35%'
pulls the crop upward, 'center 70%' downward. mobileObjectPosition
applies below 768px, where the crop is tallest. Both default to
'center'. See docs/MEDIA_WORKFLOW.md.

short paragraphs. If it grows past three paragraphs it has stopped being

config.heading: ONE LOOP, AFTER DARK
config.body:
The Kanjo is a racing game built around a single elevated expressway loop at night — a fictionalised Japanese night circuit, loosely inspired rather than reproduced.

Handling aims at believable vehicle behaviour rather than simulation for its own sake, and the interface stays deliberately minimal: the road, the traffic, and the car.

_comment: THE LATEST YOUTUBE VIDEO — resolved automatically, not pinned.
mode 'latest' resolves the channel's newest PUBLIC upload server-side:
@thekanjo -> channels.list(forHandle) -> uploads playlist ->
playlistItems.list -> newest usable item
search.list is deliberately NOT used: it costs 100 quota units against 1,
its ordering is the search index's rather than the channel's, and a fresh
upload can be missing from it for hours. See lib/youtube/client.ts.
A new upload appears here within one revalidation window (default 15
minutes, YOUTUBE_REVALIDATE_SECONDS) with NO content edit and NO deploy.
WITHOUT YOUTUBE_API_KEY — the normal state of a fresh clone — the block
renders its heading and WATCH ON YOUTUBE pointing at the channel. Nothing
fake is shown. Adding the key in Vercel later makes the video appear with
no frontend change.
mode 'pinned' + `video` keeps one specific upload on the homepage instead.
`video` is also the fallback for 'latest' if the API is ever unreachable.
poster is OPTIONAL. Without one the still comes from the API response (or
YouTube's thumbnail host), fetched by OUR server through next/image — so
the visitor's browser contacts no Google host until they press PLAY.
TIKTOK — the official Creator Profile Embed for @the_kanjo.
It shows a selection of the profile's recent videos and needs NO TikTok
developer app, no Login Kit review and no video.list authorisation,
because the profile is public and it is ours.
Nothing is scraped, nothing is proxied, and no TikTok video is downloaded
or re-hosted. The embed markup is CONSTRUCTED by our own component from a
validated handle — TikTok HTML is never accepted from this file.
embed.js is loaded once, only when the section approaches the viewport, so
it never competes with the loader or the hero.
If TikTok is blocked or slow the block shows FOLLOW ON TIKTOK instead —
that link is the embed's own initial content, not an error state.
The upgrade path to custom The Kanjo-styled cards is the TikTok Display
API (user.info.basic + video.list) and is NOT needed for V1. See
docs/TIKTOK.md.
PATREON / DEVELOPMENT LOG.
The feed comes from the official Patreon API v2 (campaigns.posts), fetched
SERVER-SIDE. There is no credential in this file and there must never be
one: the token lives in PATREON_ACCESS_TOKEN in the server environment.
See docs/PATREON.md.
WITH NO CREDENTIALS CONFIGURED — the normal state of a fresh clone — this
renders its copy and the CTA, which is what `fallback: 'cta'` means. Set it
to 'hide' to drop the block entirely instead.
showLockedPosts lists members-only posts as title + date + MEMBERS + a link.
Their bodies are NEVER rendered whatever this is set to — the excerpt is
derived from post content only when Patreon marks the post public.
campaignUrl is empty until the owner supplies the real creator page. The
section says so rather than linking somewhere invented.

_README: VIDEOS. Two reservations, both published:false, so neither renders and no
fabricated footage ships. Bring ONE live and it becomes the featured video
under the hero.
A LOCAL CLIP (provider 'file') — preferred for gameplay and cinematics,
because it ships no third-party script and no cookies:
1. export to public/media/video/ (MP4 always; WebM as well if you can)
2. export a poster frame to the same folder — MANDATORY
3. put the MP4 in `ref` and the WebM in `sources`, WebM first in
preference order
4. set "published": true
The page shows only the poster until the visitor presses PLAY; the video file
is not fetched before that. The native <video> element handles playback,
controls, fullscreen and Picture-in-Picture — no player library.
AN EXTERNAL CLIP (provider 'youtube' or 'vimeo'):
`ref` is the BARE ID, not a watch URL — 'dQw4w9WgXcQ', not
'https://youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ&list=...'. The embed URL is
composed by the site, so a pasted URL cannot smuggle in a playlist, an
autoplay parameter or a tracking string. A poster is still mandatory, and
the provider's script only loads once somebody presses PLAY.
See docs/MEDIA_WORKFLOW.md for resolution, duration, codec, bitrate and
whether to strip the audio track.

videos._note: An external alternative, for when a trailer lives on YouTube. `ref` is the bare id.

_README: SCREENSHOTS. Six reservations, all published:false, so none of them render
and no fabricated image ships. To bring one live:
1. export the capture to public/media/screenshots/ using the name below
2. write a real `alt` describing what is actually in the frame
3. set "published": true
That is the whole workflow. No component is edited, and `npm run test:media`
lists exactly which files are still missing.
`width`/`height` are the REAL pixel dimensions and are mandatory — they are
what reserves the image's space before it loads, so a wrong value shifts the
layout. 1920x1080 is the recommended export; see docs/MEDIA_WORKFLOW.md for
format, quality and the night-scene pitfalls that matter for this game.
KEEP THE SET AT ONE ASPECT RATIO. The grid reserves each cell from the
entry's own dimensions, so mixed ratios give a ragged grid — it will not
shift, but it will not read as a press set either.
`order` controls position; `featured` is available for later use and is not
read by the current layout. The filenames below are suggestions, not
requirements — the path in `image.src` is the only thing that must match.

links._comment: Addressed by id from a section's config. available:false renders the block disabled with unavailableReason shown, which is the canon's behaviour for a locked row: visible, focusable, not submittable. Nothing here invents a destination.
